title: how the co-change signal reaches an agent that never runs gs
summary: The "Edited together" partners are delivered to the agent WITHOUT it asking, at the moment an Edit/Write lands, because agents do not reliably run `gs` before editing — so until #161 the signal only reached agents who already went looking for it. The delivery path shares NO code with the `gs` rendering path: it is detector (7) inside the PostToolUse nudge handler, it reads the keeper's `cochange.json` sidecar directly, and it applies a deliberately LOOSER gate than `gs` does (ratio >= 0.3 of the seed's own commits, shared >= 2, top 5) because 'what am I forgetting' is a recall question while the `gs` cut is tuned for precision. It needs no `init` wiring at all: PostToolUse is already registered on all three hosts with a match-everything matcher, and cursor-nudge-handler delegates to the Codex one, so a new detector reaches every host for free.

UserPromptSubmit: the ONLY thing that clears the edit list
the keeper-derived sidecar the hook reads

invariants: UserPromptSubmit is the ONLY clearing signal. Elapsed time is the wrong shape for a task boundary — an auto-mode run edits for hours with no prompt, and a session id survives a resume days later. A settle clock, the session id, and a 30-min TTL were each tried and rejected as proxies for it. The 7-day sweep in resetEditTrack is garbage collection for abandoned files, never a boundary.

The nudge (PostToolUse) and the reset (UserPromptSubmit) are wired by SEPARATE init functions — wireClaudeHooks vs wireClaudeKbHooks — so a repo can have the nudge without the reset. There the list never clears; it degrades quietly rather than loudly, because each file is named at most once.
The edit list is its own tmp file, never folded into /tmp/find_nudge_<key>.json, which the search detectors and the preguard's deny-key depend on.
Hooks never import from dist/, so the hook MIRRORS getCacheDir/cacheKey. tests/cochange-nudge.test.ts asserts the two paths are equal — without it a rename on the TS side kills the feature silently.

title: how the co-change signal reaches an agent that never runs gs
summary: The "Edited together" partners are delivered to the agent WITHOUT it asking, at the moment an edit lands, because agents do not reliably run `gs` before editing. What counts as "an edit" is the load-bearing part: an edit TOOL or a deterministic shell write (`>`/`>>`, `tee`, `sed -i`, or a write call naming a literal path, via bashEditTargets in hooks/evidence.mjs). Gating on tool names alone made the whole feature silent for an agent instructed to edit with sed/heredocs/scripts — which is the auto-mode default, so the agent that most needed the nudge was the one guaranteed never to get it. The delivery path shares NO code with the `gs` rendering path: it is detector (7) inside the PostToolUse nudge handler, it reads the keeper's `cochange.json` sidecar directly, and its gate is deliberately LOOSER than `gs` (ratio >= 0.3 of the seed's own commits, shared >= 2, top 5) because "what am I forgetting" is a recall question while the `gs` cut is tuned for precision. It needs no `init` wiring: PostToolUse is registered on all three hosts with a match-everything matcher, and cursor-nudge-handler delegates to the Codex one.

steps.role: the whole feature: what counts as an edit, the per-task edit list, the gate, the message
decides which repo files a shell command WRITES — the shared table, so the nudge and the capture worklist cannot disagree
host entry — calls it as detector (7) at priority 3
pins the shell-edit shapes and the deliberate silences

invariants: only DETERMINISTIC shell writes count; a write to a computed path claims nothing. Measured: the deterministic rules cover 89.2% of real shell writes, and inferring the rest from 'the one source path in the script' added 5.8% while making it possible to name a file the script only READ
a heredoc tag is an arbitrary identifier (EOF, PATCH, TS, MSG) — never re-introduce a tag whitelist, it made whole scripts invisible
a redirect target is an edit even under a read verb, so `cat > x <<EOF` must not tier x as a read
